tasks.short: Check applicants against the vacancy requirements and refer suitable people to the recruiter.

today.trigger: An application reaches the review stage in Recruitee.
steps: Read the approved vacancy requirements and the applicant's documents.
Check stated qualifications, availability and relevant experience.
Ask for missing information and record uncertainties.
Refer applicants to the recruiter with supporting notes.
drudgery: Finding the same facts across differently formatted CVs.
Copying evidence into referral notes.
Chasing missing availability or certificate information.
today.time_sinks: Illustrative baseline to validate: 20 minutes per application, especially reading and writing referral notes; the present workflow is inferred.

lenses.faster: The assistant drafts a source-linked evidence sheet and a missing-information request, removing most copying and note writing. Allow 11 minutes for reading the evidence, checking omissions and making the referral decision against a provisional 20-minute baseline.
lenses.autonomous: A new review-stage application starts document preparation, but the administrator leads the assessment. Nothing changes the candidate's stage or sends a referral until the administrator acts.
lenses.ambitious: New service to Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo hiring managers: a referral brief that separates evidenced requirements from questions for interview. Demand would probably grow as preparing a useful brief becomes cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss retyping CV details or hunting for an availability statement. More time goes to understanding unusual experience and helping candidates explain transferable skills.
lenses.options: Show the candidate's evidence against alternative, recruiter-approved combinations of essential and trainable requirements. This can reveal that changing a vacancy requirement would widen the pool, while the recruiter decides whether the requirement should change.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts toward resolving ambiguous applications and checking referral quality. The administrator gains authority to request clarification and return incomplete vacancy criteria to the recruiter, becoming more expert in evidence and fair assessment.
reach: Absorb the Recruiter's preparation of factual referral briefs after learning structured interviewing, discrimination risks and the boundaries of applicant screening.

tasks.human_edge: The administrator recognises non-standard career paths, challenges weak job requirements and notices when missing evidence is being mistaken for lack of ability. The recruiter and hiring manager retain selection decisions.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot: applicant assessment needs a person leading the work; document preparation supports that judgment without making rankings or rejection decisions.

in_practice.trigger: The administrator opens an application in the review stage.
steps: Retrieve the vacancy version and candidate documents within the administrator's permissions.
Draft a factual evidence sheet with document references and explicit unknowns.
Have the administrator compare the sheet with the original documents and assess the requirements.
Let the administrator edit the referral or clarification request and submit it in Recruitee.
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator approves every referral and stage change; recruiter approval is required for changes to selection criteria.
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted Recruitee candidate history, recording source references, reviewer and final referral; avoid retaining duplicate CVs in model logs.

evidence.claim: Applicant screening is identified as a high-risk employment use in the EU AI Act; calling a tool a copilot does not itself settle its classification.
GDPR Article 22 constrains decisions based solely on automated processing that have legal or similarly significant effects.
The workflow and 45% saving are planning assumptions requiring a local pilot, not a documented customer result.

risks: A summary omits evidence or turns an uncertain statement into a qualification.
Assistance becomes de facto automated screening because reviewers stop checking originals.
Protected characteristics or proxies influence assessment; employment AI classification and applicable obligations need review before deployment.
Candidate documents enter an environment without suitable processing, access and retention controls.
research_questions: Does Recruitee support retrieving documents and saving reviewed notes with appropriate permissions and audit history?
In a representative sample, how often does the evidence sheet omit or misstate a requirement-relevant fact?
Does timed review save 45% after checking originals, without worsening referral quality or fairness?
What EU AI Act obligations and OR involvement apply to this precise implementation and deployment date?

tasks.short: Send applicants their approved rejection or offer and keep Recruitee up to date.

today.trigger: The recruiter or hiring manager records an approved hiring outcome.
steps: Check the decision and any approved offer details.
Choose the appropriate message or offer template.
Check the candidate, vacancy, attachments and wording.
Send the message and update the candidate record.
Follow up on delivery problems or replies.
systems: AFAS Profit where approved employment details are needed
drudgery: Copying names, vacancy details and approved terms.
Checking whether an outcome message was already sent.
Recording the same communication in multiple places.
today.time_sinks: Illustrative baseline to validate: 10 minutes per notification, including routine checks and follow-up averaged across cases.

lenses.faster: Template selection, field merging, sending and status logging disappear from routine handling. Average human work falls provisionally from 10 to 2 minutes per notification, including exceptions and sample review.
lenses.autonomous: A recorded human hiring decision and approved message inputs start the workflow. Valid routine messages send automatically; missing approvals, unusual feedback or inconsistent offer details stop the send.
lenses.ambitious: New service to candidates: outcome messages that explain the next step and name a contact, including during evening application activity. Demand for clearer follow-up would probably grow as its cost falls.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss mail merges or checking the sent folder against Recruitee. More time goes to sensitive conversations and candidates whose next step is unclear.
lenses.options: Before approving a campaign template, the recruiter compares a short outcome message with one offering specific, evidenced feedback. That choice changes the candidate experience and likely reply workload.
lenses.altitude: The administrator spends less of the week dispatching messages and more resolving delivery failures and sensitive cases. They gain authority to release validated routine notifications and stop messages with inconsistent approvals, without gaining hiring or pay-setting authority.
reach: Absorb the Recruiter's routine candidate outcome follow-up after learning feedback boundaries, offer approval rules and escalation etiquette.

tasks.human_edge: A person handles disappointment, contested feedback, negotiated terms and candidates who need a conversation. The underlying hiring decision remains with authorised people.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software: an approved decision, fixed templates and validated fields are enough to send and log most notifications; a model is unnecessary.

in_practice.trigger: An authorised recruiter records a final outcome and the required approvals in Recruitee.
steps: Validate the outcome, recipient, template version and required approvals.
Merge approved fields; attach only the approved offer where applicable.
Check for prior sends, conflicting statuses and missing information.
Send valid notifications and log delivery; route exceptions to the administrator.
Track failed delivery and candidate replies for human follow-up.
in_practice.human_gate: Human approval of the hiring outcome and offer precedes automation; the administrator handles exceptions and personalised feedback.
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee candidate history with decision approver, template version, approved attachment reference, send identifier and delivery result.

evidence.claim: Automating communication of a human-approved outcome is distinct from making a solely automated significant hiring decision.
Template merging, duplicate-send checks and event-driven dispatch can be implemented with conventional workflow software.
The 80% end-to-end saving assumes routine notifications dominate and includes exception handling; it is unmeasured at Noordhaven.

risks: An incorrect stage change triggers a premature or wrong notification.
An offer contains terms that have not been approved under the applicable CAO.
Retries send duplicate messages or the wrong attachment.
Generic wording mishandles a sensitive rejection or discloses internal feedback.
research_questions: Which Recruitee events reliably distinguish a human-approved final decision from a provisional stage change?
Can the workflow guarantee duplicate prevention and prove which approved offer was sent?
What share of messages needs personal handling, and does the resulting average remain near two minutes?
Which offer fields and template changes require recruiter, Payroll Specialist or HRBP approval?

tasks.short: Help employees use their benefits and route workplace accident or insurance paperwork.

today.trigger: An employee asks about a benefit, submits a change or needs help with workplace accident paperwork.
steps: Identify the employee, employer relationship and applicable CAO or scheme.
Check relevant employment facts and approved scheme rules.
Explain the administrative requirements and collect missing non-medical information.
Prepare the change or route the paperwork to the responsible specialist.
Record the outcome and follow up on outstanding actions.
systems: Staffing agency portals for agency-employed workers where appropriate
drudgery: Repeatedly explaining the same scheme requirements.
Checking incomplete forms and chasing missing fields.
Working out which employer or specialist should receive a request.
today.time_sinks: Illustrative baseline to validate: 20 minutes per request; complex claims and disputed entitlements can take substantially longer.

lenses.faster: Automatic scheme lookup, completeness checks and routing remove repeated searches and chasing. Allow 11 minutes instead of a provisional 20 for checking applicability, explaining the result and handling exceptions.
lenses.autonomous: A structured benefits request starts a rules-based check of employment facts and required fields. Routine guidance and reminders run automatically; disputed entitlements, financial changes and accident or insurance cases go to a person.
lenses.ambitious: New group served: night-shift employees at all three sites receive accessible scheme guidance outside office hours. Demand would probably grow when asking no longer requires contacting HR during the day.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss asking three times for the same missing form field. More time goes to helping employees navigate unfamiliar schemes and correcting unfair access problems.
lenses.options: Where scheme rules permit choices, show employee-selected scenarios such as different voluntary contribution amounts using approved calculations. The employee can compare take-home implications before choosing, with Payroll validating any pay impact.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts toward entitlement exceptions and employees who need explanation. The administrator gains authority to resolve documented administrative omissions and route cases directly, becoming more expert in CAO applicability without deciding medical or disputed legal questions.
reach: Absorb the Compensation and Benefits Specialist's routine scheme-intake and completeness checks after learning scheme eligibility, Dutch employer responsibilities and payroll handoffs.

tasks.human_edge: The administrator recognises distress, conflicting scheme interpretations and employer-boundary problems for agency workers. Specialists retain disputed entitlement, insurance, medical and payroll decisions.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software: structured intake, explicit eligibility rules and named routing paths cover the routine work; personal entitlements should come from verified calculations.

in_practice.trigger: An employee submits a structured benefits or administrative support request through an authenticated channel.
steps: Verify identity, employer relationship and the applicable versioned scheme.
Retrieve only the employment fields needed for the request and calculate routine entitlements through approved rules.
Request missing administrative fields and prepare the answer or action.
Have the administrator approve the case outcome and obtain specialist approval where required.
Record the approved action and follow up on unresolved handoffs.
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator approves case outcomes; Payroll approves pay changes, and appropriate specialists handle disputed entitlements and accident or insurance matters.
systems: Staffing agency contact or portal where authorised
in_practice.logs_to: Access-restricted AFAS case or approved HR request register, with rule version, approvals and action history; medical records remain in the appropriate separate process.

evidence.claim: SAP advertises HR assistance for payslip explanation, time off and related service workflows; this does not establish equivalent AFAS functionality.
Dutch sickness administration is rule-bound, while health information requires special-category data safeguards and should stay out of model prompts.
The proposed rules workflow and 45% saving depend on Noordhaven's actual scheme mix and exception rate.

risks: The wrong CAO or scheme version produces incorrect guidance.
An agency worker is incorrectly treated as employed by Noordhaven for a particular benefit.
Medical details enter general HR tickets or a model prompt.
Dutch accident and insurance administration is incorrectly mapped to a US workers' compensation process.
A benefits request involving sickness bypasses the established Wet verbetering poortwachter process.
research_questions: Which benefits generate the most requests, and can their eligibility rules be expressed without discretionary interpretation?
Which calculations already exist in AFAS, and which require Payroll or benefits-specialist validation?
How often do cases contain medical information, disputed entitlement or agency-employer ambiguity?
Can night-shift workers access the proposed channel, and would OR consent be required for its personal-data processing arrangements?

tasks.short: Prepare vacancy postings, publish approved versions and notify employees about internal opportunities.

today.trigger: A recruiter releases an approved vacancy for publication.
steps: Collect approved role details, location, shifts, terms and closing date.
Adapt the vacancy for the required external and internal channels.
Check wording, links and publication approvals.
Publish the vacancy and notify the eligible internal audience.
Check publication status and remove or update closed vacancies.
systems: AFAS Profit for approved internal audience fields
drudgery: Reformatting the same vacancy for several channels.
Copying location, shift and closing-date details.
Checking that stale postings have been removed.
today.time_sinks: Illustrative baseline to validate: 25 minutes per vacancy publication cycle, including channel checks and later closure.

lenses.faster: A single model step produces channel drafts from approved facts, and fixed publishing rules handle scheduling and closure. Human fact-checking and approval take a provisional 10 minutes instead of 25 across the publication cycle.
lenses.autonomous: Release of an approved vacancy starts draft preparation and channel validation. The administrator approves the publication package; approved scheduling, notification and closure then run automatically.
lenses.ambitious: New group served: flex workers receive approved routes into permanent vacancies through agreed agency channels. Demand would probably grow if relevant opportunities became easier to discover, subject to agency agreements and fair access.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss reformatting vacancy text or removing expired copies. More time goes to making shift patterns, travel expectations and entry requirements understandable.
lenses.options: Compare two factual posting variants: one leading with shifts and location, the other with training and progression. The recruiter can choose a different recruitment proposition and channel mix based on the people the vacancy needs to reach.
lenses.altitude: The administrator's week centres on publication quality and access across sites and shifts. They gain authority to stop incomplete postings and select approved channel templates, becoming more expert in accessible recruitment communication.
reach: Absorb the Recruiter's routine vacancy-channel preparation and publication checks after learning inclusive copy, recruitment channel rules and agency-to-permanent arrangements.

tasks.human_edge: The administrator understands whether a posting makes sense to a warehouse applicant and catches misleading promises about shifts, pay or training. Recruiters retain decisions about the hiring proposition and selection requirements.
tasks.pattern_why: llm_step: one call adapts approved vacancy facts into checkable channel drafts inside a predictable publication workflow.

in_practice.trigger: A recruiter marks a vacancy brief complete and approved for publication.
steps: Validate required fields and retrieve approved channel templates.
Generate channel drafts in one model call without adding terms or requirements.
Have the administrator check facts, language, audience and links and approve the package.
Publish through verified integrations and send notifications using explicit eligibility or subscription rules.
Check publication results and close postings when the vacancy closes.
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator approves every new or materially revised publication package; the recruiter approves changes to requirements or employment terms.
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee vacancy history with approved drafts, reviewer, channel identifiers, publication results and closure status.

evidence.claim: A model can adapt supplied vacancy facts into several drafts within a fixed workflow, with people checking factual and employment claims.
The digest's chatbot study reports modest work-hour savings, supporting a workflow-redesign pilot rather than assuming broad gains from access to a chatbot.
The 60% saving is a local planning estimate for preparation, approval, publishing checks and closure together.

risks: Generated wording invents benefits, pay terms or certificate requirements.
Internal notifications exclude eligible workers or use inappropriate personal profiling.
A failed channel update leaves an expired or inconsistent vacancy live.
Flex-worker outreach conflicts with agency arrangements or uses contact details without a suitable basis.
research_questions: Which required channels can Recruitee publish to and close reliably without manual duplication?
How much publication time is drafting versus approvals and channel administration?
Can all shifts and sites receive internal opportunities through channels they actually use?
What agency arrangements and privacy conditions govern notifying flex workers about permanent roles?

tasks.short: Find approved employee information and prepare a limited response for an authorised requester.

today.trigger: An employee, authorised colleague or external organisation requests information from an employee file.
steps: Verify the requester, purpose and authority to receive the information.
Identify the minimum fields or documents needed.
Search AFAS and relevant restricted personnel documents.
Check accuracy and remove information outside the approved scope.
Send securely and record the disclosure.
systems: Outlook or approved secure delivery channel
drudgery: Searching across records for standard employment facts.
Copying data into confirmation letters.
Repeating permission and disclosure checks.
today.time_sinks: Illustrative baseline to validate: 20 minutes per request; unclear authority and external disclosure checks account for much of the variability.

lenses.faster: Permission-aware field retrieval and fixed response templates replace searching and copying. The administrator spends a provisional seven minutes checking authority, scope and the prepared response instead of 20.
lenses.autonomous: An authenticated, structured request starts authority checks and preparation of a minimum-data response. No disclosure leaves the workflow until the administrator approves the recipient and scope.
lenses.ambitious: New service to employees: request a standard employment confirmation without an email exchange during HR opening hours. Demand would probably grow when obtaining a confirmation becomes simpler.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss searching several folders for a contract date. More time goes to resolving conflicting records and helping employees with unusual evidence requests.
lenses.options: Present a minimal confirmation and, only where justified, a fuller evidence package with each additional field's purpose. This changes the disclosure decision by showing when the smaller response already meets the request.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts from file hunting to disclosure judgment and correcting source records. The administrator gains authority to approve standard releases within a documented mandate and refuse excessive requests, becoming more expert in data stewardship.
reach: Absorb the Payroll Specialist's preparation of standard employment or earnings confirmations after learning which payroll figures are authoritative and when specialist sign-off is required.

tasks.human_edge: The administrator spots suspicious requests, coercion, unusual purposes and information that is technically available but inappropriate to disclose. Ambiguous authority needs human investigation.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software: structured requests, field allowlists, access checks and fixed letters solve the standard cases without a model searching entire personnel files.

in_practice.trigger: A request arrives through an authenticated intake process and is assigned a request type.
steps: Verify identity, purpose and the documented authority or other lawful basis for disclosure.
Select an approved field allowlist and retrieve current facts from the authoritative source.
Populate a fixed response and show its recipient, purpose and exact disclosed fields.
Have the administrator approve scope and obtain specialist sign-off for restricted confirmations.
Deliver through the approved channel and record the disclosure.
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator approves every disclosure; uncertain legal basis, unusual external requests and restricted pay confirmations go to the designated specialist.
systems: AFAS Profit through restricted read access
data_needed: Requester identity and verified recipient details
Authoritative employment and approved earnings fields
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted disclosure register with requester, purpose, lawful-basis reference, fields released, approver and delivery evidence.

evidence.claim: Permission checks, structured database retrieval and template generation are established deterministic software patterns.
Employee-information workflows require GDPR purpose, access and data-minimisation controls; a requester naming an employee is insufficient authority.
The seven-minute residual and 65% saving assume standard requests dominate and include review of every disclosure.

risks: An impostor obtains employment or salary information.
A broad service account exposes records beyond the administrator's rights.
A stale document overrides current AFAS facts.
Health information or unrelated personnel documents enter a standard confirmation.
A disclosure log itself retains more personal data than necessary.
research_questions: What proportion of requests fits a small set of standard confirmations with explicit field allowlists?
Can AFAS access be limited to those fields while preserving requester and reviewer audit history?
How is authority established for external organisations, and which requests must be declined or escalated?
Does seven minutes cover identity verification, scope review and secure delivery in a timed pilot?

tasks.short: Prepare reliable personnel reports and supporting documents for HR, managers and the works council.

today.trigger: A reporting deadline or an authorised request for personnel information arrives.
steps: Clarify the audience, period, definitions and permitted detail.
Gather AFAS extracts and relevant recruitment or learning data.
Reconcile totals, dates and missing records in Excel.
Prepare the report and explain material exceptions.
Obtain review and distribute to the authorised audience.
drudgery: Repeating exports and spreadsheet joins.
Reconciling inconsistent site or employee definitions.
Rebuilding the same tables and chasing explanations.
today.time_sinks: Illustrative baseline to validate: 120 minutes per recurring reporting pack; unusual requests may need separate scoping.

lenses.faster: Scheduled extracts, validated joins and fixed report layouts remove most assembly work. Allow 36 minutes for reconciliation exceptions, interpretation and approval instead of a provisional 120 minutes per pack.
lenses.autonomous: A reporting calendar starts generation after the nightly AFAS extract passes freshness and completeness checks. The administrator reviews exceptions and approves distribution; failed checks block publication.
lenses.ambitious: Decision made more often: each site's HRBP reviews onboarding gaps weekly instead of waiting for a monthly personnel pack. Demand would probably grow if a trustworthy view of week-one completion and day-90 outcomes cost little to prepare.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding spreadsheet joins or explaining conflicting headcounts. More time goes to finding the operational reason behind missing onboarding actions or inconsistent records.
lenses.options: Show vacancy cohorts by site, shift and start month alongside agreed measures of onboarding and retention. HRBPs can decide whether to change induction timing or manager follow-up rather than reacting to a single company average.
lenses.altitude: The week moves toward investigating exceptions and explaining operational patterns to site teams. The administrator gains authority to reject stale packs and require source corrections, becoming more expert in definitions and data quality.
reach: Absorb the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst's routine recurring-pack production after learning Power BI refresh controls, joins, metric definitions and privacy-safe aggregation.

tasks.human_edge: The administrator understands which apparent trend reflects a real operational problem and which reflects a transfer, late entry or changed definition. Managers and analysts retain causal interpretation and consequential workforce decisions.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software: recurring reports need reproducible calculations, reconciliations and templates; model-generated numbers would add avoidable uncertainty.

in_practice.trigger: The scheduled report date arrives and required source extracts are available.
steps: Check source timestamps, row counts, reporting period and approved definitions.
Run versioned joins, calculations and reconciliation rules.
Generate the reporting pack with source timestamps and an exception list.
Have the administrator investigate exceptions and approve the permitted audience.
Publish the approved pack and record any required source corrections.
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator approves each pack; metric changes require the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst, and sensitive interpretations go to the HRBP.
data_needed: Employment dates, site and approved shift fields
Audience permissions and small-group disclosure rules
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint report register and dataset refresh history with source timestamps, calculation version, reconciliations, exceptions and approval.

evidence.claim: Scheduled data transformation, reconciliations and templated reporting are established software capabilities; the company's existing Power BI extract provides a starting point.
The cited chatbot study reports limited work-hour savings from chatbot adoption alone; it does not demonstrate this reporting workflow's savings.
The 70% saving is a provisional estimate for recurring packs, including reconciliation and human release review.

risks: The nightly extract is presented as live information.
Incorrect joins duplicate people or mix permanent and agency populations.
Small site or shift groups reveal individual absence or other sensitive information.
Retention is reported as productivity without an agreed productivity measure.
Different cohort definitions make sites appear unfairly better or worse.
research_questions: Which recurring packs have stable definitions and consume enough time to justify automation?
Can Recruitee, AFAS and Studytube records be joined reliably without exposing unnecessary candidate or employee data?
Who records productive-at-90-days status, and how complete and comparable is that measure across sites?
How much review time remains after realistic data-quality failures and small-group suppression?

tasks.short: Keep HR documents, organisation charts, directories and forms accurate and ready to use.

today.trigger: An approved organisational, personnel, policy or CAO change requires document updates.
steps: Identify the authoritative change and affected documents.
Collect approved wording, reporting lines and effective dates.
Update charts, directories, handbooks or forms.
Check consistency and obtain the appropriate owner's approval.
Publish the new version and archive superseded copies.
drudgery: Updating the same name or reporting line in several documents.
Finding outdated copies and broken references.
Reformatting approved policy wording.
today.time_sinks: Illustrative baseline to validate: 60 minutes per document-change package; substantive policy or CAO interpretation is additional expert work.

lenses.faster: Controlled regeneration handles factual charts and directories, while one model step proposes edits to affected prose. Allow 27 minutes for checking the change set, approvals and publication instead of a provisional 60.
lenses.autonomous: An approved source change starts an impact check and prepares document revisions. The administrator verifies factual changes, and the policy owner approves substantive wording before publication.
lenses.ambitious: New service to shift supervisors: a current, site-specific starter pack with the right contacts, forms and approved policies. Demand would probably grow because supervisors could request an accurate pack without asking HR to assemble it.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss moving boxes in an organisation chart or finding obsolete handbook copies. More time goes to making instructions understandable and resolving conflicting guidance.
lenses.options: Compare a single handbook with a common core plus approved site or CAO supplements. This changes how Noordhaven maintains and presents policy, including the risk of duplication versus employees overlooking a supplement.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts toward checking change impact and maintaining usable guidance across sites. The administrator gains authority to withdraw obsolete copies and return contradictory instructions to their owners, becoming more expert in document governance and plain-language communication.
reach: Absorb the HRBP's preparation of routine policy amendments after learning CAO interpretation boundaries, approval ownership and when OR consent or consultation must precede release.

tasks.human_edge: The administrator notices when formally consistent wording will confuse a shift worker or conflict with local practice. HR policy owners, legal advisers and the OR retain their respective substantive and statutory roles.
tasks.pattern_why: llm_step: one call proposes source-linked edits for varied documents; deterministic generation handles factual charts and directories, and fixed approvals control publication.

in_practice.trigger: An approved AFAS organisational change or signed-off policy change enters the document-change register.
steps: Identify affected documents through a maintained source-to-document register.
Regenerate factual sections and use one model call to draft prose edits with source references.
Run checks for stale dates, unresolved references and inconsistent terminology.
Have the administrator review the comparison and obtain policy-owner and required governance approvals.
Publish versioned documents, archive obsolete versions and notify affected audiences.
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator approves factual updates; substantive policy wording requires its owner, with required OR procedures completed before implementation.
data_needed: Approved organisational facts and effective dates
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint version history and document-change register with source change, comparison, reviewer, approvals, effective date and publication status.

evidence.claim: SixFifty advertises handbook and contract workflows grounded in an attorney-maintained rules base; its US legal content does not establish Dutch CAO compliance.
The Coca-Cola Andina case emphasises structured content and named HR knowledge owners as practical requirements for reliable HR answers.
The 55% saving is an estimate for maintaining documents after the underlying change is approved, including review and publication.

risks: A paraphrase changes the meaning of a CAO provision or policy.
Unapproved policy changes are published as administrative updates.
Incorrect source reporting lines spread into several documents.
Site copies remain accessible after replacement.
A directory exposes personal contact details to an unnecessarily broad audience.
research_questions: Which documents can be generated from AFAS facts, and which contain substantive policy judgment?
Are document owners, dependencies and authoritative versions identifiable today?
What changes require OR consent or consultation, and can release be blocked until that process is complete?
In a pilot, how often do generated edits alter meaning or miss dependent documents, and does review still fit 27 minutes?

role.altitude: The HR Administrator becomes the operational steward of accurate personnel actions, safe disclosures and usable HR information across three sites. The two administrators spend more of their week investigating exceptions, helping employees and checking that approved actions reach the right systems; they gain bounded release and stop-work authority rather than hiring, pay-setting or policy-making authority.
reach: Recruiter: factual referral briefs, routine outcome follow-up and vacancy publication administration.
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: routine scheme intake, completeness checking and approved-rule explanations.
Payroll Specialist: preparation of standard employment and earnings confirmations, with required payroll validation.
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: production and reconciliation of established recurring HR packs.
HR Business Partner: preparation of routine policy amendments and current supervisor starter packs.
role.ceiling_note: These seven tasks cover about 424 hours per administrator annually, roughly 26.5% of the supplied role time. The provisional savings total about 252 hours per administrator, or 505 hours across two FTE, worth approximately EUR 24,200 in annual capacity at EUR 48/hour; this is not a measured saving or an automatic payroll reduction. Exceptions, source-data quality, integration access, approval delays and the remaining role tasks limit further gains.
skills_to_grow: AFAS and Recruitee workflow administration, permissions and audit trails.
CAO applicability and boundaries between administrative interpretation and specialist advice.
AVG/GDPR disclosure judgment, data minimisation and secure handling of candidate and employee records.
Employment AI classification, meaningful human review and applicable EU AI Act obligations.
Power BI definitions, reconciliation and privacy-safe reporting.
SharePoint versioning, plain-language guidance and document dependency management.
Sensitive employee and candidate conversations and effective specialist escalation.
Pilot measurement that includes checking, corrections, exception work and downstream rework.
role.ambitious_version: Run a dependable HR administration service for every site and shift, with timely candidate communication, complete starter information and early identification of onboarding gaps. After validating the component workflows, pilot an employee-facing front door on approved content with deterministic personal-entitlement lookups and human escalation; establish necessary OR consent, access controls and AI disclosure before launch. Judge success through dossier readiness, week-one onboarding and contribution to productive hires still present at day 90, alongside errors and employee experience.
